title: ArtifactArena: Evaluating Models by What They Build in the Physical World
abstract: arXiv:2610.06511v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: To evaluate the frontier, we must measure models not by what they say, but by what they can engineer and build in grounded physical environments. We introduce ArtifactArena, an open-ended platform where models face a physically grounded hardware-software co-design challenge: engineering fully functional robots to compete in a simulated arena. We evaluate a frontier model's zero-shot, verifier guided refinement, and open-ended physical design capabilities through three harnesses that refine their bot artifacts based on text descriptions, physics simulator feedback, and gameplay data. We benchmark these capabilities with an Elo ranking of frontier models derived from head-to-head tournaments between their artifacts. translated_title: ArtifactArena：通过模型在物理世界中构建的成果来评估模型
translated_abstract: 要评估前沿水平，我们不能仅凭模型说了什么来衡量，而要看它们能在真实的物理环境中工程化并构建出什么。我们提出 ArtifactArena——一个开放式平台，模型在其中面临一项物理落地的软硬件协同设计挑战：工程化制造功能完备的机器人，在模拟竞技场中展开竞赛。我们通过三种评估框架来考察前沿模型的零样本能力、验证器引导的迭代改进能力以及开放式物理设计能力，这些框架分别基于文本描述、物理模拟器反馈和对战数据来改进其机器人作品。我们通过机器人作品之间的面对面锦标赛得出前沿模型的 Elo 排名，以此对这些能力进行基准测试。通过发布这一框架与锦标赛基础设施以支持社区的持续提交，我们建立了一个活的、不会被饱和的测试平台，持续测量开放式智能不断扩展的边界。
tldr: ArtifactArena 提出一个开放式测试平台，通过让模型设计制造功能完备的机器人在模拟竞技场中实际对战并以 Elo 排名评测，来衡量模型在物理世界中的开放式工程与设计能力。
en_tdlr: ArtifactArena introduces an open-ended testbed that evaluates models' open-ended engineering and physical design capabilities by having them build functional robots that compete head-to-head in a simulated arena, ranked via an Elo system.
